attributes.law_screen: offsetof-fused-immediate-counter: APPLIED -- this is the core technique used at all 25 converted sites: replace a bare hex/decimal displacement with a compile-time offsetof() expression added to (or, for vmu_exists's off-256 site, subtracted-with-a-stride-term from) the SAME raw pointer as a single additive/subtractive expression, never a typed intermediate. offsetof-rename-preserves-protected-web: APPLIED, the primary confirming precedent for the whole pass -- every site kept the original raw pointer's declared type and the single-additive-expression shape, and this held byte-identical across EXACT fns (add_vmu_file, InitPreferences, vmu_exists), a RELOCATION_ONLY fn (saveSave), and STRUCTURAL fns with previously-documented fragile register webs (buildSaveImage, loadGauntletSave -- both have capped register-web-closure attempts from earlier today) alike. declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast: screened, not applicable -- no typed intermediate alias variable was introduced at any site; every base pointer kept its original raw type throughout, so this law's 'declare one alias' counter-form was never needed. large-fn-batch-fuzzy-can-mask-subfield-regression: screened, not applicable -- no function in this TU is anywhere near the ~4000-insn fuzzy-arbitration threshold (largest is loadGauntletSave at 857 insns), so fndiff real/--count was the correct and sufficient arbitration metric, checked after every function via defake_gate.py. lwzu-idiom-web-retention: screened, applicable in spirit to vmu_exists's off/entry directory-scan walk, but the conversion used offsetof-on-the-SAME-raw-pointer with no typed intermediate, so the web-splitting mechanism (a cast through a differently-typed pointer) never triggered; vmu_exists held real 0. multifield-alias-defeats-indexed-addressing v2: screened, applicable in spirit to several multi-field bases (add_vmu_file's rec, buildSaveImage's hi/hi2/sizeHi touching 5 SaveImageHeader fields), but since no typed alias or array-index form was introduced anywhere (every site kept the raw pointer type, only the displacement literal changed), the law's actual regression mechanism never applied; all these functions held real/insns exactly. offsetof-overturns-typed-alias-caps: screened, not applicable -- no prior attempt record caps a de-fakematch conversion specifically on this TU's raw-cast sites (the existing capped/parked records here are all register-web/scheduling-closure attempts from ordinary matching work, a different axis), so there was no typed-alias cap to re-attempt with offsetof. offsetof-rename-array-member-boundary: screened -- checked every rename base against this law's array-member-decay hazard; all 25 sites use a POINTER-VARIABLE base (rec, e, base, lbl_80343C74, q, entry, hi/hi2/sizeHi, win, tex[0]), never a raw pointer obtained by `->` decay through an array-typed struct member, so the boundary this law found does not apply here. pointer-walk-array-index-regression / recomputed-index-array-form-safe: screened, not applicable -- no walked-loop pointer was converted to array-style indexing anywhere in this pass; vmu_exists's off/entry walk stayed a raw pointer-plus-offsetof expression throughout. scalar-read-write-lfsu-mixed-form: screened, not applicable -- no adjacent same-address scalar read-then-write pair was touched (the closest candidate, buildSaveImage's bannerFmt byte, is read/written across widely separated statements and branches, not an immediately adjacent fusion-sensitive pair). walked-base-symbol-identity: screened, not applicable -- every converted site keeps referencing its ORIGINAL base symbol/pointer unchanged; no site was rewritten to reference a different global than the one the target's own relocations already use, so the two-overlapping-symbols hazard never arises.
